course_name_original: Fundamentals of Computer Graphics and Image Processing
course_name_en: Fundamentals of Computer Graphics and Image Processing

learning_outcomes.text: The graduate will master the basic techniques of image processing, such as basic image transformations, basic techniques of image preprocessing (image filtering, edge detection), basic principles of segmentation.

The graduate is familiar with the basics of modeling and rendering procedures, computer animation and multimedia, can implement selected graphics algorithms and understands their mathematical background.

syllabus_topics: Rendering of 3D graphics, calculation of light and shadows, photorealism
Modeling techniques (box modeling, parametric modeling, procedural)
Computer animation (keyframe technique, tweening, procedural animation)
Color spaces, additive and subtractive color models. Color depth
Raster and vector graphics. 2D graphic formats
Multimedia, 2D image compression, video compression, codecs
Computer graphics applications: industrial and graphic design, computer games, virtual reality, scientific visualization
assessment_rules: To successfully complete the course, students must obtain at least 50% of points on the exercise assignments and at least 50% on the final exam. The final grade is calculated as follows: A for 90%, B for 80%, C for 70%, D for 60%, E for 50%. The assessment is based on 50% continuing evaluation and 50% exam.
bibliography: Digital image processing / Rafael C. Gonzalez, Richard E. Woods. Upper Saddle River : Prentice-Hall, 2002
Hughes: Computer Graphics Principles and Practice, ISBN: 978-0-321399-52-6
institution: Univerzita Komenského v Bratislave (Comenius University Bratislava)
degree: Bachelor Applied Informatics (1-AIN), Faculty of Mathematics, Physics and Informatics
